content.title: What is the Internet of Things (IoT)? Benefits, Challenges & Applications
content.text: Challenges Of IoT: Risks And Roadblocks To Consider The flexibility and possibility of IoT come with significant challenges. With a well-designed threat detection and response system in place, however, an organization can meet the following obstacles head on. 1. Data interception and exploitation The data that goes between IoT devices and the cloud can be intercepted by bad actors and then used to extort companies or sold to the highest bidder. This includes users’ personal information, medical records, and identities. 2. Devices as breach opportunities Every connected device is a potential entry point for a hacker. They can be used as a convenient access point for a network or to introduce malware. 3. Compromised devices affecting the manufacturing process Because IoT devices can control the critical machines a manufacturer uses, they need to be carefully secured. 4. Interruption or hacking of critical infrastructure More and more, IoT is becoming incorporated in transportation, chemical refineries, energy grids, and other critical elements of everyday infrastructure. If these were hacked, pivotal services could be interrupted. 5. Security-related challenges Some of the challenges faced by IoT are not necessarily new, but the way they affect IoT devices is unique. An increase of botnets: A botnet is a string of internet-connected devices that hackers implement to remotely control IoT devices and use them for illegal activity. The more IoT permeates business, the more botnet attacks there will be. Lack of encryption: Many IoT devices do not have the storage or processing capabilities that would enable them to take advantage of the kinds of encryption that computers use. This can leave their data exposed to hackers. Hackers can then manipulate the security protocols that were supposed to protect the IoT device. Weak passwords: Many devices come with default passwords that are weak and easy to figure out. If users fail to change the default passwords as soon as the device is installed, they can be especially vulnerable to attacks. Phishing attacks: IoT devices are the largest attack vector of phishing attacks, which is when an email is used to trick someone into opening and installing malware. Once a phishing attack has implanted malicious software, a hacker can send a signal to the IoT device to disable or control it. User privacy: Many IoT devices use user information to individualize the experiences they provide. Hacking into an IoT device can gain a malicious actor access to a treasure trove of personal data. Why Is IoT Considered A Game-Changing Technology? In recent years, IoT has been gaining popularity as businesses begin to realize its potential to increase efficiency and productivity. A recent study found that the number of IoT devices will grow from 9.7 billion in 2020 to 29 billion by 2030. This growth is being driven by the falling cost of sensors and the increasing demand for connected devices. Here are some of the most important trends that will impact the IoT space in the next five years: 1. Increased adoption of IoT devices As sensors continue to become cheaper, more businesses and consumers will be able to afford IoT devices. This will lead to increased adoption of IoT devices and a corresponding increase in the amount of data collected and exchanged. 2. Increased investment in IoT As the potential of IoT is realized, more businesses will be willing to invest in the technology. This will lead to increased research and development, as well as more funding for startups working on innovative IoT solutions. Global spending on IoT is likely to reach $1.2 trillion by 2025. 3. Growth of the IoT platform market As IoT adoption increases, so will the demand for platforms that can manage and analyze the data generated by IoT devices. The global IoT platform market is expected to reach $7.3 billion by 2028. 4. Increased focus on security As more and more devices connect to the internet, security will become a top priority for businesses and consumers. This will lead to increased investment in security solutions and the development of new standards for IoT security. 5. Expansion of 5G networks The rollout of 5G networks will have a major impact on the IoT space. 5G is expected to provide higher speeds and lower latency, which will enable new applications such as autonomous vehicles, augmented reality (AR), and virtual reality (VR). The Future Of IoT: Key Trends And Emerging Innovations IoT is set to transform the way systems operate, offering benefits such as improved efficiency, intelligent automation, and real-time decision-making across sectors. As technology advances, several key trends are shaping the future of IoT: AI integration: AI enhances IoT systems by analyzing data to enable automation and intelligent decision-making. Impact of 5G: 5G networks support faster data transfer and massive device connectivity, enabling real-time IoT applications. Increased device connectivity: The rise in connected devices generates valuable data to boost efficiency and service innovation. Advancements in smart cities: IoT powers smart cities by using sensors to manage traffic, energy, and public safety efficiently.
